The Commandments of Christ · His own commandments: one another · 46–63

← Repent, Believe, Follow  ·  The Commandments of Christ: all subjects  ·  Prayer, Fasting and Giving →

The new commandment and what follows from it: mercy, forgiveness, service, and care for the least.

On this page: The New Commandment · Judging and Forgiving · Serving · The Little Ones and the Poor

The New Commandment

46. A new commandment: to love one another as He has loved you.

I give you a new commandment: that you love one another. Just as I have loved you, you also are to love one another. By this everyone will know that you are My disciples, if you have love among one another.”

John 13:34–35

See also: John 15:12 · John 15:17
In the Law: 79. Love of neighbor and refusal of revenge

47. To be merciful, as your Father is merciful.

Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.

Luke 6:36

In the Law: 115. Doing what is right in God’s sight

48. To love your enemies, do good, and lend expecting nothing back.

But love your enemies, do good, and lend, expecting nothing back. Your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High, because He is kind to the ungrateful and evil.

Luke 6:35

See also: Matthew 5:44
In the Law: 36. Lending without exploiting the needy

49. Go, and do likewise: to show mercy as the Samaritan did.

Which of these three seems to you to have become a neighbor to the man who fell among the robbers?” He said, “The one who showed him mercy.” Jesus said to him, “Go, and you do likewise.”

Luke 10:36–37

In the Law: 79. Love of neighbor and refusal of revenge

Judging and Forgiving

50. Not to judge, so that you are not judged; first to take the beam out of your own eye.

Do not judge, so that you may not be judged. For with the judgment you use, you will be judged, and with the measure you use, it will be measured to you. Why do you see the splinter in your brother’s eye, but do not notice the beam in your own eye? Or how will you say to your brother, ‘Let me remove the splinter from your eye,’ when behold, the beam is in your own eye? Hypocrite! First remove the beam from your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the splinter from your brother’s eye.

Matthew 7:1–5

See also: Luke 6:37–38 · Luke 6:41–42

51. To forgive, so that your Father may forgive you.

For if you forgive people their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you. But if you do not forgive people, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.

Matthew 6:14–15

See also: Mark 11:25 · Luke 6:37
In the Law: 79. Love of neighbor and refusal of revenge

52. To forgive your brother not seven times but seventy times seven.

Then Peter came and said to Him, “Lord, how often will my brother sin against me and I forgive him? Up to seven times?” Jesus says to him, “I tell you, not up to seven times, but up to seventy times seven.

Matthew 18:21–22

See also: Luke 17:3–4
In the Law: 78. Correcting a neighbor responsibly · 79. Love of neighbor and refusal of revenge

53. If your brother sins, to show him his fault between you and him alone; then with one or two others; then to tell it to the church.

If your brother sins against you, go and reprove him between you and him alone. If he hears you, you have gained your brother. But if he does not hear, take one or two more with you, so that every matter may be established upon the mouth of two or three witnesses. If he refuses to hear them, tell the Church. And if he refuses to hear even the Church, let him be to you like the Gentile and the tax collector.

Matthew 18:15–17

In the Law: 78. Correcting a neighbor responsibly · 137. Corroborated testimony in serious cases

Serving

54. Whoever wishes to be great among you shall be your servant, as the Son of Man came to serve.

It shall not be so among you. Instead, whoever wishes to become great among you will be your servant, and whoever wishes to be first among you will be your slave, just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve and to give His life as a ransom in place of many.”

Matthew 20:26–28

See also: Mark 10:43–45 · Luke 22:26–27 · Matthew 23:11–12

55. To wash one another’s feet, as He has done.

So if I, the Lord and the Teacher, washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet. For I have given you an example, so that you also may do just as I did to you.

John 13:14–15

56. To take the last place, for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled.

But when you are invited, go and recline in the last place, so that when the one who invited you comes, he will say to you, ‘Friend, move up higher.’ Then you will have honor before all who recline at table with you. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”

Luke 14:10–11

See also: Luke 18:14

57. When you have done everything commanded, to say, We are unprofitable slaves.

So you also, when you have done everything commanded you, say, ‘We are unprofitable slaves; we have done what we ought to have done.’”

Luke 17:10

58. Not to be called Rabbi, father or guide, for you are all brothers.

But you shall not be called ‘Rabbi,’ for One is your Teacher, and you are all brothers. And call no one upon earth your father, for One is your Father, the heavenly One. Nor shall you be called guides, because One is your Guide, the Christ.

Matthew 23:8–10

The Little Ones and the Poor

59. To let the children come to Him and not hinder them.

When Jesus saw it, He was indignant and said to them, “Let the children come to Me; do not stop them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.

Mark 10:14

See also: Matthew 19:14 · Luke 18:16

60. Not to despise one of these little ones, nor cause one of them to stumble.

See that you do not despise one of these little ones, for I tell you that their angels in the heavens continually see the face of My Father in the heavens.

Matthew 18:10

See also: Matthew 18:6 · Mark 9:42 · Luke 17:1–2
In the Law: 75. Respect and protection for disabled people

61. When you give a feast, to invite the poor, the crippled, the lame and the blind.

He also said to the one who had invited Him, “When you give a midday meal or a supper, do not invite your friends or your brothers or your relatives or rich neighbors, lest they also invite you in return and you receive repayment. But when you give a reception, invite the poor, the disabled, the lame, and the blind. And you will be blessed, because they have nothing with which to repay you; for you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.”

Luke 14:12–14

In the Law: 132. Opening the hand to a poor neighbor

62. What you did to one of the least of these His brothers, you did to Him.

The King will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, insofar as you did it to one of the least of these My brothers, you did it to Me.’

Matthew 25:40

In the Law: 132. Opening the hand to a poor neighbor

63. To have salt in yourselves and be at peace with one another.

Salt is good; but if salt becomes saltless, with what will you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”

Mark 9:50
